statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low, with index futures halted for the entire forecast window.
recommendation: Tail stays well below the block threshold across all 24 forecast hours because every one of them falls inside the CME weekend halt. The last observed structure was a completed retracement into Friday's close, not repeated extension. The elevated Stress reading describes a steep long end, Brent above 100 dollars and a disrupted Strait of Hormuz rather than an observed one-way Nasdaq-100 path. The first opportunity for fresh price-path evidence is the Sunday futures restart at 22:00Z, which lies beyond this window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 weekend halt: Tail low after Friday's record probe was fully retraced; long-end yields, Brent above 100 and Hormuz disruption keep Stress elevated
body: Friday closed the Nasdaq-100 at 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% and a record close, after probing an intraday record of 31,017.53 and then giving back roughly 210 points to finish near the session low of 30,737.07. That completed retracement, rather than a shallow pullback or repeated extension after a failed retracement, is the last observed price structure and is evidence against mean-reversion failure. September payrolls of 29,000 against expectations near 90,000, unemployment at 4.2%, average hourly earnings up 0.1% on the month and a downward revision of August to 133,000 cut priced odds of an October rate hike to about 16% from roughly 64% a week earlier. The advance was narrow and tech-led: the Nasdaq-100 at 1.00% outpaced the S&P 500 at about 0.73% and the Dow at 0.49%, while Nvidia set an intraday record of 237.87 dollars on an additional 150 billion dollar buyback authorisation that lifts its remaining programme to 235 billion dollars. VIX fell 6.59% to 15.31, settling at the low of its 15.30 to 16.24 range. The backdrop nevertheless stays difficult. Treasury yields reversed higher despite the soft labour data, with the 10-year up about 4 basis points to 5.28% on Friday and the latest H.15 column showing the 2-year near 4.78%, the 10-year near 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61%. WTI settled at 91.11 dollars after an intraday one-month low of 88.06 and a recovery on G7 emergency reserve-release plans, with Brent near 102.25. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed, with one transit recorded on 27 September against a baseline near 85 per day and about 148 vessels anchored in the monitoring zone, and UK maritime authorities reported two tankers struck on Friday with no casualties and both vessels continuing. That is incremental escalation rather than a discontinuity. CME equity-index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, beyond this horizon, so no mechanism for sustained mean-reversion failure exists inside the forecast window. Confidence is high because verified settlement levels, the session range, VIX, the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year curve, energy settlements, the payroll actuals and the seven-day U.S. calendar are all in hand; the only material limitation is the absence of any live price path during the halt, and the shared Finviz context file was stale and only partially collected, so it was not used as evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the second half of Friday's payroll session and the opening stretch of the weekend halt. Tail sat at 22 through the European morning, rose to 24 into the 12:30Z payroll release and then to 25 and 27 across the 13:30Z cash open as the index gapped up and extended toward its record, which lifted the mapped state to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES for two hours. It fell back to the watch band from 15:00Z once that advance faded from the intraday high and the retracement completed. From 21:00Z, with futures closed, Tail declined steadily from 14 to 6 and the mapped state returned to EA_ON, while Stress eased from the high band near 79 to 60 and the dominant mode settled to normal. All 24 slots are available from published Claude assessments.
outlookSummary: All 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, since index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, beyond this horizon. With no tradeable session and therefore no mechanism for sustained mean-reversion failure, Tail is projected to hold between 4 and 5 and the mapped state stays EA_ON throughout, with no danger window published. Stress eases from 59 toward a trough near 55 through Saturday evening as realised volatility stays at zero, then firms back toward 59 into Sunday morning as unresolved long-end yield, Brent and Strait of Hormuz inputs end the window exactly as unresolved as they began. Confidence decays slowly from 87 to 80 because the newest available price observation ages past a full day and no venue can refresh it before the window closes. The weekday cash-open and closing-stretch checkpoints do not apply on a weekend, and the first high-impact scheduled catalysts, ISM Services on 5 October and the FOMC minutes on 7 October, fall well beyond this window.
